craft_notes: Sthāyin: wonder at radiance (thousand-sun close of the song). Sanskrit first: span (up-down), pair (sun-moon), affirmation (truly), blaze (thousand-sun) → L4 sets span+pair line 1, affirmation+blaze line 2. Rows: row 1 (predicate-last — blaze closes as prabhā closes); row 8 (high vowels noon/blaze). Rupture: dash-colon after 'moon' — cosmos held, then burning. Close: end-weight on noon (the brightest word last). Minimal pass: 'at noon' added (thousand suns imply midday; time-word singable, no doctrine). Read aloud: line 1 spans wide (above/below), line 2 burns long (blazes/bright/thousand). Rejected: 'like a thousand suns' simile-softened — killed: -prabhā is radiance-possession, keep the blaze blunt; exclamation — killed: colon crowns.

lines: Above, below, her state abides — sun joined with moon:
truly she blazes, bright as a thousand suns at noon.
l4.sanskrit_cite: ūrdhvādho 'vasthitāvasthā sūryācandramasāv ubhau / satyaṃ virājamānā sā sahasrārkasamaprabhā

reads_against.argmap: She abides spanning up and down, sun and moon both, thousand-sun radiant.
c1_essence: Her abiding spans high and low, sun and moon, thousand-sun bright.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta with vīra-utsāha (wonder braced by resolve)
